statusText: Tail 14% (low), Stress 37% (moderate), Confidence 84% (high). Mapped policy state: EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON and Tail remains well below the block threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the U.S. cash open, 13:30-15:00 UTC, where an already-aligned bullish overnight regime carries the highest opening-continuation risk. Outside that window the overnight advance is modest, volatility is subdued and mean reversion has not been denied. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures grind to another session high on oil relief and Trump-Xi summit optimism, with volatility still subdued
body: NQ front-month trades 30,242.50, up 1.09% and about seven points under the 30,249.75 session high, a third consecutive hourly extension off the 29,904.00 overnight low; Investing.com shows the same contract at 30,238.25 on a 05:18 EDT delayed quote, so the level is corroborated. The 345.75-point (1.16%) range is modest and no failed-retracement sequence has been observed, so the advance still reads as an orderly one-way drift rather than a mean-reversion failure. The repeated extension to fresh highs while price holds within ten points of the session extreme is the genuine amplifier and lifts Tail one point to 14. Cash ^NDX closed Friday at 29,644.17, up 0.67%, at the top of its 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below the 30,762.20 52-week high, with semiconductors leading. Cross-asset context is supportive rather than stressed: VIX is 14.97, up 1.08%, in a 14.90-14.99 range; WTI trades near $98.05 to $98.59, down roughly 1.7% to 2.2% in a fourth consecutive session of decline as Strait of Hormuz flows at six-month highs and reported U.S.-Iran message exchanges around the UN General Assembly unwind the supply premium; Brent is near $101.67 to $102.00. Preliminary U.S.-China talks in New York ahead of Thursday's Trump-Xi summit were described by the U.S. Treasury Secretary as very successful, with the November tariff-truce expiry and semiconductor export-licensing language the specific levers most cited. Against that, the rate backdrop stays genuinely tight after the Fed's September 16 hike: the 10-year yield closed Friday near the 5.00% area after backing up about seven basis points, and the H.15 release through September 17 shows the 2-year at 4.67% and the 10-year at 4.94%. Rising yields alongside a tech-led bid is a cross-asset conflict, which raises Stress and caps Confidence rather than raising Tail. Stress is held at 37 and Confidence lifted to 84 on two independent live futures quotes, live VIX and oil, and a calendar corroborated by two sources. The shared Finviz context file is 3.9 hours old with collectionStatus partial and futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was treated as unhealthy and excluded from this assessment; all evidence above comes from independent current research. Scheduled checkpoints inside the horizon are the 10:30 UTC Goolsbee speech and the 12:30 UTC Chicago Fed activity index, neither of which had printed at the assessment cutoff.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail stayed in a 5-13 band and Stress in a 30-37 band throughout, with every slot mapped to EA_ON and green. Dominant mode was normal for 21 slots and turned trend-up in the final three, once the futures advance off 29,904.00 became directionally efficient enough to register. Tail drifted from 5 up to 9 between 22:00 and 01:00 UTC as the reopen set direction, eased back to 5 by 05:00 UTC, then stepped to 11, 12 and 13 in the last three hours. Confidence improved steadily from 70 to 83 as overnight evidence accumulated. No slot approached the block threshold.
outlookSummary: The conditional path keeps Tail inside the low band across all 24 hours, peaking at 19 in the first full hour after the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open, where an aligned bullish overnight regime carries the session's highest opening-continuation risk, then decaying to 9 through the post-close, maintenance-break and Asian hours before ticking back to 12 by Tuesday's European morning. Stress peaks near 44 at the open and eases to 31 overnight, staying in the moderate band throughout. Confidence declines with horizon from 84 to 65. Scheduled checkpoints inside the horizon are the 10:30 UTC Goolsbee speech and the 12:30 UTC Chicago Fed activity index; beyond it are Tuesday's Richmond Fed index with the Williams, Jefferson and Barkin speeches, the September 23 flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC, claims and new home sales on September 24, and durable goods on September 25. Thursday's Trump-Xi summit and continued Middle East diplomacy around the UN General Assembly are the main unscheduled headline levers, with the trade-truce tariff cap expiring in early November still unresolved.
